sasha: Heads-up — ZettaCompute asked for a joint perf/W run next Wed. Goal: compare our default runtime vs their kernel-tuned build on 8x A100-80GB. Can we commit lab time?

lee: I can own kernel tuning + kernel-level perf counters. Need precise CUDA + driver versions and a power-cap plan.

maria: I'll own the metric deck: throughput (tok/s), tail latency p95/p99, perf per watt (tokens / joule), and cost proxy. Need exact workloads (chat vs completion) and batch distributions.

kevin: Zetta wants a marketplace announcement after the paper. We'll need a joint data table and a short joint blurb. Marketing wants rough numbers within 48h post-run.

lee: Ops questions: do we run with persistent KV cache warmup? I'd prefer 2 phases: cold start (empty cache) and warmed (3k tokens prefix). Also set power cap to 250W, 300W, and no-cap for comparison.

sasha: Agreed. Maria — can you produce the harness that runs both phases and emits per-epoch energy (W*s) so perf/W is tokens / joules?

maria: Yes. I'll use ipmi + nvidia-smi polling at 1s and aggregate. Bench harness will emit CSV with columns: run_id, model, batch_size, seq_len, tokens, seconds, joules, tok_per_joule, p95_ms, p99_ms.

bench-bot: Scheduled run -> run_id=zetta-2026-03-25-a ; command: 
```
bench run --target a100-8x --model redwood-7b --batch-profile "chat: [1,2,4], completion: [8,16]" --warmup 300 --power-caps 250,300,0 --collect-energy ipmi,nvidia-smi --report csv
```

lee: For kernel tuning I want: CUDA 12.2, driver 535.xx, TensorRT 8.7, cuDNN 9.2. If Zetta has a patched kernel, we need the exact git commit + diff. Also collect perf counters: sm_efficiency, l2_hit_rate, dram_util.

kevin: @sasha can you confirm Zetta's hardware spec + who from their side will be the contact? They mentioned "dwight" as the eng lead.

sasha: Confirmed — Zetta contact is dwight (dwight@zettacompute.com). Hardware: 8x A100-80GB NVLink, Mellanox HDR IB, Ubuntu 22.04, BMC access for telemetry. I'll loop him in after we finalize the plan.

oliver: One ask from product: include a 99% confidence interval for tokens/sec so we don't overclaim in the announcement. Also please capture model output quality (sanity prompts) to ensure kernel changes don't regress results.

maria: Good call. I'll add a small eval set (50 prompts) and compute rough ROUGE+perplexity deltas. If any regression > 0.5% we'll flag and require retest.

lee: Quick config snippet for kernel flags I'll try: 
```
# kernel.cfg excerpt
export CUDA_HOME=/usr/local/cuda-12.2
export LD_PRELOAD=/opt/zkernel/libzktune.so
export ZKERNEL_TUNE=aggressive
echo 0 > /proc/sys/kernel/printk # reduce noise
```

bench-bot: Note: lab booking holds for 2026-03-25 09:00-15:00 UTC. Please ack to lock.

sasha: Ack from me. @lee @maria @kevin please ack and add any missing measurements by EOD today so I can share the final run plan with dwight. :thumbsup:

lee: Ack.

maria: Ack — adding eval and CSV schema to the repo now.

kevin: Ack. I'll prepare a one-pager template for the joint announcement and a table schema for marketing numbers.

sasha: Thanks team. I'll DM dwight and cc kevin once we freeze the plan.
